findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not also the owner (and an owner who is not also returned as admin) fails the check and gets FORBIDDEN unless they are the booking user or an attendee. The bookings UI treats admin and owner as alternative roles (isUserTeamAdminOrOwner), so team admins cannot add guests on bookings they are allowed to manage.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the actor's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees is run with EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking already loads booking.user.credentials, but they are ignored. When a team admin or an attendee (both explicitly authorized) adds guests, the organizer's calendar event is updated with the wrong user's integrations, so the invite is not updated on the host calendar (or is applied to the actor's calendar). Guests are already written to the DB before this call, so a failure also leaves attendees and calendars out of sync.

findings.title: Guest dedupe and blacklist are case-sensitive
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but each guest is compared with includes(guest) and with attendee.email using strict equality. Zod's email() does not normalize case, so a blocked address submitted with different casing bypasses the blacklist, and the same person can be inserted again as another attendee (duplicate calendar invites and emails).

findings.title: Emails are keyed off the raw guest list, not the guests actually added
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the original input, not uniqueGuests. In sendAddGuestsEmails, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new-booking confirmation with a fresh invite) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee, or a case-mismatched address that was filtered out of the insert, therefore sends the wrong email and ICS to people who were already on the booking.

findings.title: No status, seat, or capacity checks before inserting attendees
findings.body: The handler updates any booking by id after the permission check. Cancelled, rejected, and pending bookings can gain attendees, and seated event types (seatsPerTimeSlot is only copied onto the calendar payload) get extra Attendee rows with empty names and no seat reference or capacity check. That overbooks the slot, breaks seat-based cancel/reschedule (which keys off seatsReferences), and still triggers calendar updates and emails.

findings.title: Custom email title/subject are overwritten by props spread
findings.body: Both AttendeeAddGuestsEmail and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail set title, subject, headerType, and (organizer) callToAction, then spread {...props} afterward. Those props are ComponentProps of the scheduled-email components, which already include title/subject/callToAction. Any caller or renderEmail default that passes those fields replaces new_guests_added / guests_added_event_type_subject / callToAction={null}, so the HTML body is a normal scheduled-event email instead of a guests-added notice. Put the overrides after the spread.
